subjects.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
clues: Born in Bonn in 1770, he moved to Vienna as a young man and stayed there for life.
One of his teachers in Vienna was the composer Joseph Haydn.
He kept composing great music after losing almost all of his hearing.
His Ninth Symphony ends with a choir singing the 'Ode to Joy'.
The deaf German composer of Fur Elise and the da-da-da-DUM Fifth Symphony.
subjects.fact: The 'Ode to Joy' melody from his Ninth Symphony is used as the anthem of the European Union.

subjects.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
clues: As a child prodigy he toured the royal courts of Europe with his father and sister.
He was writing his first little pieces of music at about the age of five.
His operas include The Magic Flute and The Marriage of Figaro.
He wrote more than 600 works before dying at just 35 in Vienna.
The Austrian composer from Salzburg who wrote Eine kleine Nachtmusik.
subjects.fact: The 1984 film Amadeus, about his life, won eight Oscars including Best Picture.

subjects.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
clues: Born in 1685 into a large family of musicians in central Germany.
He spent his last 27 years as music director of a church school in Leipzig.
He had 20 children, and several of his sons became composers too.
He wrote more than 200 surviving church cantatas for Sunday services.
The great Baroque organist who wrote the Brandenburg Concertos and Goldberg Variations.

links.name: George Frideric Handel
links.rel: was born the same year as

subjects.fact: As a young man he walked about 400 km to Lubeck to hear the famous organist Buxtehude play.

subjects.name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
clues: Born in 1840, he studied law and worked as a government clerk before turning to music.
He was among the very first students of his country's first music conservatory.
In 1891 he conducted at the opening festival of Carnegie Hall in New York.
His 1812 Overture is famous for its booming cannon fire.
The Russian composer of the ballets Swan Lake and The Nutcracker.
subjects.fact: The Nutcracker features the celesta, a bell-like keyboard instrument he discovered in Paris.

subjects.name: Frédéric Chopin
clues: Born near Warsaw in 1810, he was giving public concerts as a young boy.
He left his homeland at 20 and spent most of his short life in Paris.
Nearly every piece he wrote features the solo piano.
He wrote many mazurkas and polonaises, dances from his home country.
The Polish 'poet of the piano', famous for his nocturnes and etudes.
subjects.fact: At his request, his heart was taken back to Warsaw, where it rests in a pillar of the Holy Cross Church.

subjects.name: Antonio Vivaldi
clues: Born in 1678, he trained as a priest and was nicknamed for his red hair.
For decades he taught music at an orphanage whose all-girl orchestra was famous.
He wrote hundreds of concertos, many of them for the violin.
He died poor in Vienna in 1741, far from his home city of canals.
The Baroque composer from Venice who wrote The Four Seasons.
subjects.fact: Much of his music was forgotten for about 200 years and only rediscovered in the 20th century.

subjects.name: George Frideric Handel
clues: Born in 1685 in Halle, he shares his birth year with another Baroque giant.
He spent most of his career in London, writing operas for its theatres.
He wrote his Water Music for a royal boat party on the River Thames.
His anthem Zadok the Priest has been sung at every British coronation since 1727.
The composer of the oratorio Messiah, with its famous Hallelujah chorus.

links.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
links.rel: was born the same year as

subjects.fact: Audiences traditionally stand up during the Hallelujah chorus.

subjects.name: A. R. Rahman
clues: Born in Chennai in 1967, he played keyboards in bands as a teenager to help his family.
He composed music for advertising jingles before moving into films.
His first film score, for the 1992 Tamil movie Roja, made him a star.
He won two Oscars in 2009 for the music of Slumdog Millionaire.
The Indian composer behind the song Jai Ho, nicknamed the Mozart of Madras.
subjects.fact: He was born A. S. Dileep Kumar and changed his name in his early twenties.

subjects.name: The Beatles
clues: Formed in 1960, they sharpened their act playing long nightclub sets in Hamburg.
Their drummer Pete Best was replaced by Ringo Starr in 1962.
Their 1964 arrival in the United States set off a wave of screaming fan hysteria.
Their albums include Abbey Road and Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band.
The four lads from Liverpool: John, Paul, George and Ringo.
subjects.fact: Their last public concert was an unannounced show on a London rooftop in January 1969.

subjects.name: Queen
clues: This British rock band formed in London in 1970.
Their guitarist built his own electric guitar with his father, using wood from an old fireplace.
That same guitarist later earned a PhD in astrophysics.
Their 1985 Live Aid set at Wembley is often called one of the greatest live shows ever.
The band of Freddie Mercury, famous for Bohemian Rhapsody and We Will Rock You.
subjects.fact: Bohemian Rhapsody runs nearly six minutes and has no repeating chorus.

subjects.name: The Rolling Stones
clues: Formed in London in 1962, they were sold as the rebellious rivals of a Liverpool band.
Their singer and guitarist first met as schoolboys in Dartford, Kent.
Their tongue-and-lips logo is one of the most famous in music.
Mick Jagger and Keith Richards wrote most of their songs.
The band behind (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction and Paint It Black.
subjects.fact: In 2022 they celebrated 60 years as a band with a European tour.

subjects.name: Led Zeppelin
clues: This English hard-rock band formed in London in 1968.
Their guitarist Jimmy Page had earlier played in the Yardbirds.
Their name came from a joke that they would go down like a lead balloon.
They split up in 1980 after the death of their drummer, John Bonham.
The band of singer Robert Plant, behind Stairway to Heaven and Whole Lotta Love.

subjects.name: Nirvana
clues: Formed in Aberdeen, Washington, in 1987, they became the face of grunge music.
Their drummer Dave Grohl later founded the Foo Fighters.
In 1992 their album Nevermind replaced Michael Jackson's Dangerous at number one in the US.
The cover of Nevermind shows a baby swimming towards a dollar bill on a fishhook.
The Seattle grunge band of Kurt Cobain and Smells Like Teen Spirit.

links.name: Michael Jackson
links.rel: knocked off the top of the chart

subjects.fact: The band's name refers to the Buddhist idea of perfect peace and freedom.

subjects.name: U2
clues: Formed in 1976 after a teenage drummer pinned a notice on his Dublin school board.
Their guitarist is known simply as The Edge.
Their 1987 album The Joshua Tree made them global superstars.
In 2014 their album appeared free in about 500 million iTunes accounts, surprising many users.
The Irish rock band fronted by Bono, singer of With or Without You.

subjects.name: Coldplay
clues: Formed in London in 1997 by four students at University College London.
Their breakthrough single in 2000 shared its name with a colour.
They headlined the Super Bowl 50 halftime show in 2016.
Their 2008 hit Viva la Vida took its title from a Frida Kahlo painting.
The British band of Chris Martin, behind Yellow, Clocks and Fix You.

links.name: Frida Kahlo
links.rel: named a song after a painting by

subjects.name: Pink Floyd
clues: Formed in London in 1965, they began in the psychedelic scene with Syd Barrett.
Their 1973 album spent more than 900 weeks on the US Billboard 200 chart.
Their concerts famously featured a giant inflatable flying pig.
Their rock opera The Wall tells of a rock star who shuts himself off from the world.
The band of The Dark Side of the Moon, with its prism-and-rainbow cover.

subjects.name: AC/DC
clues: Formed in Sydney in 1973 by two Scottish-born brothers, Malcolm and Angus Young.
Their lead guitarist famously performs dressed in a school uniform.
Their singer Bon Scott died in 1980 and was replaced by Brian Johnson.
Their 1980 album Back in Black is one of the best-selling albums of all time.
The Australian hard-rock band of Highway to Hell and Thunderstruck.
subjects.fact: The band's name came from a label on a sewing machine, meaning both kinds of electric current.

subjects.name: ABBA
clues: This pop group formed in Stockholm in 1972.
The group was made up of two married couples.
Its name is made from the first letters of its four members' first names.
They won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with Waterloo.
The Swedish quartet behind Dancing Queen and the songs of Mamma Mia!
subjects.fact: In 2022 digital avatars of the four members began performing in the London show ABBA Voyage.

subjects.name: Spice Girls
clues: This British group was put together in 1994 after an advert in a showbiz newspaper.
A pop magazine gave each member a nickname, such as Baby, Sporty and Posh.
Their 1996 debut single topped the charts in dozens of countries.
Their slogan celebrated the strength and friendship of young women.
The five-member pop group behind Wannabe, including Victoria Beckham.

subjects.name: BTS
clues: This seven-member group debuted in Seoul in 2013 on a small record label.
In 2018 their leader gave a speech at the United Nations about loving yourself.
Their devoted fans are known as the ARMY.
Their 2020 song Dynamite was their first all-English single and a US number one.
The K-pop band of RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jungkook.

subjects.name: Blackpink
clues: This four-member group debuted in Seoul in 2016.
One of its members, Lisa, was born in Thailand.
Their 2018 hit Ddu-Du Ddu-Du became a huge YouTube success.
In 2019 they became the first K-pop girl group to play the Coachella festival.
The K-pop group of Jisoo, Jennie, Rose and Lisa.

subjects.name: One Direction
clues: This group was formed in 2010 on a British TV talent show.
Its five members each auditioned as solo singers and were grouped by the judges.
They finished only third on The X Factor but became far bigger than the winner.
They began an extended break in 2016, and Harry Styles went on to solo stardom.
The boy band behind What Makes You Beautiful and Story of My Life.

subjects.name: Eminem
clues: Born in 1972, he grew up mostly in and around Detroit, often moving home.
He was discovered by the producer Dr. Dre, who signed him in 1998.
He played a character based on himself in the 2002 film 8 Mile.
His Lose Yourself was the first rap song to win the Oscar for Best Original Song.
The Detroit rapper whose alter ego is called Slim Shady.

subjects.name: Tupac Shakur
clues: Born in New York in 1971, he studied acting and poetry at a Baltimore arts school.
He moved to California as a teenager and found fame on the West Coast.
His 1995 single Dear Mama was a heartfelt tribute to his mother.
He also acted in films such as Juice and Poetic Justice.
The West Coast rapper of California Love and Changes, who died at 25 in 1996.
subjects.fact: In 2010 Dear Mama was added to the US Library of Congress National Recording Registry.

subjects.name: Jay-Z
clues: Born in 1969, he grew up in the Marcy Houses in Brooklyn.
He co-founded the record label Roc-A-Fella Records in 1995.
In 2017 he became the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
He is married to Beyonce.
The Brooklyn rapper of Empire State of Mind and 99 Problems.

subjects.name: Snoop Dogg
clues: Born in Long Beach, California, in 1971.
He was introduced to the world on Dr. Dre's 1992 album The Chronic.
He co-hosted a TV cooking show with the homemaking star Martha Stewart.
He was a cheerful TV correspondent at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris.
The laid-back West Coast rapper of Drop It Like It's Hot, known for his '-izzle' slang.

subjects.name: Drake
clues: Born in Toronto in 1986, he first became known as a teenage actor.
He played a basketball player in the Canadian TV drama Degrassi: The Next Generation.
He signed to Lil Wayne's label Young Money in 2009.
His 2016 hit One Dance topped the charts in many countries.
The Canadian rapper of Hotline Bling and God's Plan.

subjects.name: Kendrick Lamar
clues: Born in 1987, he grew up in Compton, California.
His 2012 album good kid, m.A.A.d city told stories of growing up in his city.
In 2018 he became the first rapper to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music.
He headlined the Super Bowl halftime show in New Orleans in February 2025.
The Compton rapper of HUMBLE. and Alright.

subjects.name: Jimi Hendrix
clues: Born in Seattle in 1942, he taught himself to play guitar as a teenager.
He was left-handed and often played a right-handed guitar flipped upside down.
He became a star in London in 1966 with his trio, the Experience.
His closing set at Woodstock in 1969 included a wild Star-Spangled Banner.
The guitar hero of Purple Haze who set his guitar on fire on stage.

subjects.name: Eric Clapton
clues: Born in Surrey, England, in 1945, he was raised by his grandparents.
He played in the Yardbirds and then in the power trio Cream.
Graffiti in 1960s London famously declared that he was 'God'.
He is the only person inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame three times.
The British guitarist nicknamed Slowhand, who wrote Layla.

subjects.name: Carlos Santana
clues: Born in Jalisco in 1947, he learned violin from his father before switching to guitar.
As a teenager he played in clubs in Tijuana before moving to San Francisco.
His band's 1969 Woodstock set made them famous before their first album came out.
His 1999 album Supernatural earned him eight Grammy Awards in one night.
The Mexican-born guitarist of Smooth and Oye Como Va.

subjects.name: B.B. King
clues: Born on a Mississippi cotton plantation in 1925.
He started out as a radio DJ in Memphis, Tennessee.
He named every guitar Lucille, after a dance-hall fire he ran back into to save one.
He toured tirelessly, playing hundreds of concerts a year well into old age.
The blues guitar legend crowned the King of the Blues.

subjects.name: Louis Armstrong
clues: Born in New Orleans in 1901, he learned to play the cornet at a boys' home.
His nicknames included Satchmo and Pops.
His gravelly voice helped make scat singing popular.
In 1964 his Hello, Dolly! knocked the Beatles off the top of the US chart.
The jazz trumpeter who sang What a Wonderful World.

links.name: The Beatles
links.rel: knocked off the top of the chart

subjects.name: Miles Davis
clues: Born in Illinois in 1926, he moved to New York to study at the Juilliard School.
As a young man he played trumpet with the bebop pioneer Charlie Parker.
He reinvented his style many times, from cool jazz to jazz-rock fusion.
His 1959 album Kind of Blue is often called the best-selling jazz record ever.
The cool jazz trumpeter behind Kind of Blue and So What.

subjects.name: Duke Ellington
clues: Born in Washington, D.C., in 1899, he earned his noble-sounding nickname as a stylish boy.
His orchestra became famous playing at Harlem's Cotton Club from 1927.
He wrote well over a thousand compositions during his career.
Take the 'A' Train, written by his partner Billy Strayhorn, became his band's theme.
The jazz bandleader and pianist of Mood Indigo and It Don't Mean a Thing.

subjects.name: Ella Fitzgerald
clues: Born in Virginia in 1917, she grew up in Yonkers, New York.
At 17 she won an amateur night contest at Harlem's Apollo Theater.
She recorded famous 'songbook' albums of great American songwriters.
She won more than a dozen Grammy Awards and was called the First Lady of Song.
The jazz singer celebrated for her scat, who sang A-Tisket, A-Tasket.

subjects.name: Elvis Presley
clues: Born in Tupelo, Mississippi, in 1935; his twin brother died at birth.
He recorded his first songs at Sun Studio in Memphis.
He served in the US Army in Germany from 1958 to 1960.
His Memphis mansion, Graceland, is now a museum.
The King of Rock and Roll, who sang Hound Dog and Jailhouse Rock.

subjects.name: Michael Jackson
clues: Born in Gary, Indiana, in 1958, the eighth of ten children.
He began singing as a small boy in a family group with four of his older brothers.
He first showed off the moonwalk dance on TV in 1983.
His 1982 album Thriller is the best-selling album of all time.
The King of Pop, who sang Billie Jean and Beat It.

subjects.name: Madonna
clues: Born in Bay City, Michigan, in 1958, she moved to New York with little money to dance.
She starred as Eva Peron in the 1996 film musical Evita.
Her 1990 hit Vogue was inspired by a dance style from New York clubs.
In 2024 she played a free concert on Copacabana Beach in Rio to over a million people.
The Queen of Pop, who sang Like a Prayer and Material Girl.

links.name: Rio de Janeiro
links.rel: gave a giant free concert in

subjects.name: Whitney Houston
clues: Born in Newark, New Jersey, in 1963, she sang in her church's gospel choir as a girl.
Her mother Cissy was a gospel singer and her cousin was Dionne Warwick.
She starred alongside Kevin Costner in the 1992 film The Bodyguard.
Her 1991 Super Bowl performance of the US national anthem became a hit single.
The singer of I Will Always Love You and I Wanna Dance with Somebody.

subjects.name: Freddie Mercury
clues: Born on the island of Zanzibar in 1946, he went to boarding school in India.
He studied graphic art and design in London and designed his band's crest.
On stage he famously sang into a short, bottomless microphone stand.
At Live Aid in 1985 he led about 72,000 fans in call-and-response singing.
The flamboyant lead singer of Queen who wrote Bohemian Rhapsody.

subjects.name: Bob Marley
clues: Born in a Jamaican village in 1945, he moved to Kingston's Trenchtown as a boy.
He formed the Wailers with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer.
Time magazine named his 1977 album Exodus the album of the century.
He spread reggae music and the Rastafari faith around the world.
The reggae legend who sang One Love and No Woman, No Cry.

subjects.name: Shakira
clues: Born in Barranquilla in 1977, she wrote her first song at the age of eight.
Her father has Lebanese roots, and she learned belly dancing as a child.
Her song Waka Waka was the official song of the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
She co-headlined the 2020 Super Bowl halftime show with Jennifer Lopez.
The Colombian singer of Hips Don't Lie and Whenever, Wherever.

subjects.name: Taylor Swift
clues: Born in Pennsylvania in 1989, she moved to the Nashville area at 14 to chase country music.
She started as a country singer before going fully pop with an album named after her birth year.
In 2021 she began re-recording her early albums to control her own music.
By its end in 2024, her Eras Tour was the highest-grossing concert tour ever.
The singer-songwriter of Love Story, Shake It Off and Anti-Hero.

subjects.name: Beyoncé
clues: Born in Houston, Texas, in 1981, she entered talent shows as a young girl.
She first found fame as lead singer of the girl group Destiny's Child.
Her husband is the rapper Jay-Z.
By 2025 she had won more Grammy Awards than any other artist.
The singer of Crazy in Love and Single Ladies, known as Queen Bey.

subjects.name: Adele
clues: Born in London in 1988, she studied at the BRIT School for performing arts.
Her albums are named after her age when she made them, such as 19, 21 and 25.
Her album 21 helped her win six Grammy Awards in a single night in 2012.
She won an Oscar for the theme song of the James Bond film Skyfall.
The London singer of Rolling in the Deep, Someone Like You and Hello.

subjects.name: Frank Sinatra
clues: Born in Hoboken, New Jersey, in 1915, the son of immigrants from Italy.
He sang with the big bands of Harry James and Tommy Dorsey before going solo.
He won an Oscar for his acting role in From Here to Eternity.
His nickname was Ol' Blue Eyes, and he led the famous 'Rat Pack' of entertainers.
The crooner who sang My Way and New York, New York.

subjects.name: Édith Piaf
clues: Born in Paris in 1915, she spent part of her childhood with her grandmother.
She began her career singing for coins on the streets of the French capital.
Her stage name was slang for 'sparrow', a nod to her tiny size.
She stood only about 1.42 metres tall but had a huge, powerful voice.
The French singer of La Vie en rose and Non, je ne regrette rien.

subjects.name: Lata Mangeshkar
clues: Born in Indore in 1929, she began singing professionally at 13 after her father died.
Her younger sister Asha Bhosle also became a famous singer.
She recorded thousands of songs in more than 30 languages over seven decades.
In 2001 she received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.
Known as the Nightingale of India, she was Bollywood's most famous playback singer.

subjects.name: Fela Kuti
clues: Born in Abeokuta in 1938, he went to London to study music.
His mother was a pioneering campaigner for women's rights.
He blended West African highlife with jazz and funk.
His songs boldly criticised his country's military rulers.
The Nigerian bandleader and singer who pioneered Afrobeat in Lagos.

subjects.name: Bob Dylan
clues: Born in Duluth, Minnesota, in 1941, he moved to New York at 19 to play folk clubs.
He shocked folk fans by playing an electric guitar at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival.
His songs include Blowin' in the Wind and The Times They Are a-Changin'.
In 2016 he became the first songwriter to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
The harmonica-playing singer-songwriter of Like a Rolling Stone.

subjects.name: Bad Bunny
clues: Born in 1994, he was bagging groceries at a supermarket when his music took off.
He first shared his songs by uploading them to SoundCloud.
His 2020 album El Ultimo Tour del Mundo was the first all-Spanish album to top the Billboard 200.
He was Spotify's most-streamed artist in the world from 2020 to 2022.
The Puerto Rican star of reggaeton and Latin trap, known for Dakiti.
